record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.context_brief: Count of stratum types for arbitrary n
record.original_question: Determine, as a function of n, how many different types of strata can occur in tensegrity configuration spaces on n labeled points.

evidence.quote: A stratum is by definition a maximal connected component of B_d(G) with equivalent fibers.
Problem 3 Compute the number of different types of strata for n points with arbitrary n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be a positive integer and consider configurations of $n$ labeled points in general position in the plane (or in Euclidean space of fixed dimension $d$). A tensegrity framework on $n$ points is given by a graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ together with a self-stress: an assignment of real weights $w_{ij}$ to the edges $ij$ of $G$ such that at every vertex $i$ the equilibrium condition $\sum_{j:\,ij\in E(G)} w_{ij}(p_j - p_i) = 0$ holds, where $p_1,\dots,p_n$ are the positions of the points.

For a fixed graph $G$, let $B_d(G)$ denote the space of point configurations $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ admitting a nonzero self-stress on $G$, equipped with the natural "fiber" structure assigning to each configuration the linear space of all self-stresses supported on $G$. A stratum is defined to be a maximal connected subset of $B_d(G)$ on which the fibers (the spaces of admissible self-stresses, viewed up to the relevant equivalence) are equivalent. Two strata, possibly arising from different graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices, are said to have the same type if they are equivalent under the natural notion of stratum equivalence (so that strata coming from different graphs may coincide as types).

Determine, as an explicit function of $n$, the total number of distinct types of strata that can occur across all tensegrity configuration spaces on $n$ labeled points.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as an open problem in the survey on configuration spaces of tensegrities published in the Arnold Mathematical Journal (2018). Codimension-1 strata have been classified for n ≤ 8, with partial information for n = 9 and unknown strata appearing at n = 10. No closed-form count as a function of n appears to be known.
